answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before receiving one job slot. The bond is an anchor tying access to scarce capital: a plume of fresh accounts gives an attacker no free capacity, because each account needs its own deposit. Flooding this digital garden with 10,000 identities at $100 per bond ties up $1 million for a month, imposing financing costs even if every bond is later returned.
